systolic array.definition: A grid of multiply-accumulate cells through which data is pumped in rhythmic beats; each input is read from memory once and reused across many cells, trading memory traffic for throughput.

mxu.definition: Matrix Multiply Unit — the systolic array at the heart of a TPU TensorCore, classically a 128×128 grid of MACs (16,384 multipliers) that computes one 128×128 matrix-multiply tile per pass.

mac.definition: Multiply-accumulate — the primitive a systolic cell performs each beat: multiply an activation by a stored weight and add it to the running partial sum (acc += a × w).

tensorcore.definition: The compute core of a TPU chip: one or more MXUs (matrix units) plus a vector unit and scalar unit, fed from HBM.

hbm.definition: High-Bandwidth Memory — the fast on-package DRAM that feeds a TPU's compute units (≈95 GB at ≈2.8 TB/s on v5p).

arithmetic intensity.definition: FLOPs performed per byte read from memory. High intensity (lots of reuse) keeps a chip compute-bound; low intensity leaves it memory-bound and idle.

bf16.definition: bfloat16 — a 16-bit float with fp32's full 8-bit exponent range but fewer mantissa bits. Halves the bytes moved versus fp32 while staying stable for training; the default matmul type on TPUs.

weight-stationary.definition: A systolic dataflow that loads weights into the array once and holds them put while activations stream through — maximising weight reuse.

asic.definition: Application-Specific Integrated Circuit — a chip designed for one job. A TPU is an ASIC purpose-built for the matrix math in neural networks; it can't run general-purpose code.

vpu.definition: Vector unit — the part of a TensorCore that handles non-matmul math (activations, softmax, normalization, elementwise ops), alongside the MXU and scalar unit.

tpu vm.definition: The Linux host VM physically attached to the TPU chips. You SSH in with root access and run your JAX / PyTorch-XLA code; it dispatches the heavy compute to the TPU over PCIe.

ici.definition: Inter-Chip Interconnect — the high-bandwidth links wiring TPU chips into a slice and Pod (a 3D torus), bypassing the host network. Collective operations ride ICI.

multislice.definition: Joining multiple slices/Pods over the slower Data-Center Network (DCN) for jobs bigger than one Pod — cross-slice traffic is far slower than ICI.

sparsecore.definition: A dedicated TPU unit (introduced on v4; on v5p, v6e, v7 and the training-focused TPU 8t) that accelerates very large embedding lookups — the heavy part of recommendation/ranking and MoE routing. On the inference-focused TPU 8i it is replaced by a CAE.

cae.definition: Collectives Acceleration Engine — the TPU 8i (inference) block that replaces the four SparseCores; aggregates results across cores with near-zero latency, cutting on-chip collective latency ~5× (key for fast auto-regressive decoding).

tpu 8t.definition: Google's 8th-generation training TPU — SparseCores + an LLM decoder engine on a 3D-torus network, native FP4, 216 GB HBM; superpods of 9,600 chips scaling past a million per cluster.

tpu 8i.definition: Google's 8th-generation inference TPU — replaces SparseCores with a CAE, carries 3× the on-chip SRAM (384 MB) to hold the KV cache, and uses the Boardfly network; tuned for serving/reasoning.

boardfly.definition: TPU 8i's network topology — a hierarchical optical-circuit-switched design with a ~7-hop diameter across 1,024 chips (vs 16 on a 3D torus), ~56% lower than a torus.

liquid cooling.definition: Introduced at TPU V3 — the fix when rising performance density broke air cooling. Liquid carries heat away so chips can run hotter/denser.

ocs.definition: Optical Circuit Switch — introduced at TPU V4. Reconfigurable optical links that reshape slices and route around failed chips; the only way to wire very large Pods reliably.

trillium.definition: The TPU v6e generation — cost-efficient, tuned for inference and smaller training runs; ≈100× the performance of V2.

ironwood.definition: The 7th-gen TPU (v7 / TPU7x). Ships in two pod sizes — 256 and 9,216 chips; 9,216 is the megascale maximum.

padding.definition: XLA zero-pads tensor dimensions up to the MXU tile (128, or 256 on v6e/v7) and the memory lanes (multiples of 8/128). Misaligned shapes carry wasted padded zeros — burning compute and on-chip memory, a common cause of surprise OOMs.

fp4.definition: Native 4-bit floating point on TPU 8t — halves the bytes per parameter versus bf16, roughly doubling MXU throughput by cutting memory traffic per FLOP.
